title: Inquest into police shooting that killed a Londoner coming in February
subtitle: More than three years after he was shot and killed by police in Waterloo, an inquest into the death of Beau Baker is tentatively set for early next year.
article: More than three years after he was shot and killed by police in Waterloo, an inquest into the death of Beau Baker is tentatively set for early next year.

Though the exact date and location of the inquest will be released at a later date, it's expected to take place February 2019 in Kitchener-Waterloo, Office of the Chief Coroner spokesperson Julia Noonan-Savage said Thursday.
The 20-year-old London native was shot seven times by a Waterloo Regional police officer after he was found wielding a knife outside his Kitchener apartment April 2, 2015.
In an October 2015 report, Ontario's Special Investigations Unit (SIU) declined to press charges against the unnamed officer involved in Baker's death.
The arm's length agency investigates reports involving police where there has been death, serious injury or allegations of sexual assault.
An inquest into Baker's death was first announced in August 2016.
Setting a date for the proceedings was delayed because the case is complex and had many different parties involved, Noonan-Savage said.
The inquest will examine the events surrounding Baker's death and the jury may make recommendations designed to prevent similar deaths from happening.
